create.title: Literal shifted-divisor charts and target-safe phase-free double-far mode
create.statement_tex: For every persistent literal balanced block, the double-far divisor coefficient has the exact charts rho=[h^2(n+r)-h'^2 n]/(hh'), r=hq+kp+pq, rho=hq-kp, r+rho=q(2h+p), and r-rho=p(2k+q). Nonzero terms have p=2s and chi_4(h)chi_4(h+p)=(-1)^s. In angular variables rho=2sqrt(n(n+r))sinh(t-t'), while the fixed-shift phase Hessian has determinant -(qx-py)^2/[16{xy(x+p)(y+q)}^(3/2)]. The fully assembled phase-free double-far aggregate M_B^(0)=sum_df a_B^<(h,k)conj(a_B^<(h',k')) satisfies |M_B^(0)|<<_epsilon L^3X^epsilon by divisor expansion and character summation with both gcd weights, both slanted symbols, and both far gates retained. Hence E_(B,df)=M_B^(0)+R_B^osc and the actual energy target is equivalent modulo a target-safe term to the oscillatory zero-subtracted remainder. No absolute value over shifts, residues, divisors, or shells is permitted in the phase-free lemma.
create.next_action: Use the phase-free term only after full signed assembly. Attack the oscillatory zero-subtracted remainder jointly; residuewise, shiftwise, divisorwise, or shellwise absolute values discard the proved saving.

create.title: Oscillatory zero-subtracted double-far actual-symbol remainder
create.statement_tex: For every persistent j=1 literal balanced block at L asymp X^(1/6), prove |R_B^osc|<<_epsilon L^3X^epsilon, where R_B^osc=sum_df a_B^<(h,k)conj(a_B^<(h',k'))[e(sqrt X(sqrt(hk)-sqrt(h'k')))-1], and df means |h'k'-hk|>L and |hk'-h'k|>L. Both chi_4 factors, both low-gcd weights, both literal slanted symbols, floors, support crossings, and the fixed physical block remain inside the joint sum. The bracket is not pointwise small. By M9-M2-balanced-double-far-phase-free-mode-reduction this estimate is equivalent up to a target-safe term to M9-M2-balanced-double-far-actual-energy.
create.next_action: Name and prove a joint signed nonzero-alias or local-energy inequality retaining the determinant projector and all actual weights. Do not repeat owner-amplified Fejer, outer B-process self-return, or continuous-Hessian-only arguments.

create.title: Fejer owner amplification and critical outer-transform self-return
create.statement_tex: Let b_n=c_B(n)e(sqrt(Xn)) have product support length N_B asymp L^2. The exact Fejer inequality has prefactor P_H=(N_B+H-1)/H and positive form Gamma(0)+2Re sum_(1<=r<H)(1-r/H)Gamma(r). For 2<=H<=L, the accepted radial-corridor allowance becomes O_epsilon(L^4X^epsilon) after P_H. For L<=H<=N_B, either complete O(L^3) corridor supplies only O_epsilon((L^5/H+L^3)X^epsilon). Thus existing owners certify no fixed-power shortening H<=L^(2-delta); H=L^(2-o(1)) retains the full power shift range. A two-dimensional Fejer window has the same area amplification. The determinant gate is pair-dependent and has no supplied positive-semidefinite scalar factorization. At the critical scale the outer B-process has dual length L^2, unit stationary amplitude, and reciprocal phase X/(4m); the p=2s character shifts rather than deletes nonzero aliases; continuous determinant-Hessian nondegeneracy is not a discrete modulo-one estimate. This obstructs these mechanisms with existing owners, but is not a lower bound and does not reject a new signed local-energy theorem.
create.next_action: Do not reuse target-saturating corridor owners after a shortened Fejer lift. Continue only with a genuinely new signed local-energy or joint nonzero-alias theorem, or park the route.

reject.reason: For p=2s, chi_4(h)chi_4(h+p)=(-1)^s is constant in h. Any factor-L saving must be assembled across shifts or aliases, not attributed to fixed-shift inner character oscillation.
The zero-frequency Poisson summand remains; only its interior critical point is absent on the relevant bulk. A full nonzero half-shifted stationary family and boundary terms remain.
The exact Hessian determinant proves continuous nondegeneracy proportional to rho^2. It does not count integer aliases, prove injectivity or lattice discrepancy, or give modulo-one cancellation.
The Fejer prefactor is asymptotic to L^2/H. It amplifies either target-saturating corridor to allowance L^5/H; existing owners certify target safety only at full power length H=L^(2-o(1)).
The determinant gate depends on the two divisor representatives inside c_B(n+r)conj(c_B(n)), not only on n and r. No positive-semidefinite scalar factorization is supplied.
At n asymp L^2 and R asymp L^3, the dual length is again L^2, stationary amplitude is order one, and the Legendre phase is X/(4m). The bare transform is capacity-preserving.
Cowan's stated theorem has incompatible prime-level, even-character, nontrivial-product, nonzero-power, and fixed-parameter hypotheses, and lacks the literal truncations, gates, and coupled weight.

Chamizo treats the complete r_2 correlation, not the literal balanced coefficient. Even its hardest-range displayed fixed-shift error exceeds the L^3 energy budget after a triangle sum over L^2 shifts.
